interest: Shows an interned Austrian engineer offering Japanese metallurgical intelligence, and Bern intercepts of Japanese coal and mineral claims.
overview: Docket (1942-43) for file 894.63: Langdon reports interned engineer Hansgirg could provide intelligence on Japan's light-metals industry; Harrison in Bern relays Japanese Coal Control's expanded-output claims and a Tokyo press report on strategic mineral gains.

people.name: Fritz Hansgirg
people.role: Austrian inventor and metallurgist detained in an internment camp

people.name: William R. Langdon
people.role: State Department official, Division of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: A State Department index sheet recording papers 21 and 22 concerning Japanese light metals, electro-chemical industries, and coal output in 1942.
subfiles.summary: Langdon's 1942 memo notes interned engineer Hansgirg could supply intelligence on Japan's light metals; Harrison's telegram relays Japanese coal-output claims.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: 894.63, Sub-numbers 21-22

subfiles.about: A State Department index sheet recording paper 23 regarding reported production increases in Japanese strategic minerals in 1943.
subfiles.summary: Harrison's 1943 Bern telegram relays a Tokyo press report on increased Japanese strategic mineral production.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: 894.63, Sub-number 23
